# Apply for a research grant or innovation award

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

When a defined research or innovation project may fit a published funding opportunity. A submitted eligible application or documented no-go, with award conditions separated from funding assumptions.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. Qualified advisers own legal, tax, safety or regulatory determinations and any required professional work. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

> Editorial status: operational draft. Source pages checked on 2026-10-29. No case-specific legal review, professional assurance or completed execution is claimed.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Match the actual project to published opportunities

agent-runnable


Record the official sponsor, call, applicant rules, project scope, submission date and eligible costs. Distinguish grants from loans and procurement contracts, and reject offers that cannot be verified through the sponsor.

- Sources: [SBA grants](https://www.sba.gov/loans/additional-funding-opportunities/grants/)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Confirm eligibility and the funding commitment

human · human approval required


The project owner and finance adviser check entity, geography, research and matching-fund conditions. Decide whether the project can proceed if no award is made; an application is not cash or permission to incur reimbursable costs.

- Sources: [SBA grants](https://www.sba.gov/loans/additional-funding-opportunities/grants/)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Prepare the technical, budget and delivery proposal

agent-runnable


Write the research question, milestones, team capability, evidence and cost basis against the published criteria. Make assumptions and subcontractor dependencies explicit and reconcile totals across the application forms.

- Sources: [SBA grants](https://www.sba.gov/loans/additional-funding-opportunities/grants/)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Approve and submit the application

manual form/portal · human approval required · hard to undo


The authorized applicant checks certifications, budget and final attachments before submitting through the official portal. Retain the submitted copy and receipt and keep requested clarification work in an owned register.

- Sources: [SBA grants](https://www.sba.gov/loans/additional-funding-opportunities/grants/)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Assess the award decision and accept conditions

human · human approval required


Review the actual award terms, restrictions, milestones, IP provisions and reporting with advisers. Obtain authority before acceptance and hand the agreement to the grant-compliance owner rather than treating selection as unrestricted revenue.

- Verify: A submitted eligible application or documented no-go, with award conditions separated from funding assumptions.
- Sources: [SBA grants](https://www.sba.gov/loans/additional-funding-opportunities/grants/)
